description: Hand-labelled ground truth for the dolevf/DVGA external target (GraphQL JWT-identity authorization bypass). Each probe is driven through the real GraphQlBolaValidator by bench-dvga. A probe matches a runner observation on (operation, object_id, attacker_profile). expected_label is what the validator MUST conclude. The two decoys are realistic operations a naive cross-id scanner would flag but that are actually safe.

vulnerabilities.rationale: core/helpers.py:20-21 (get_identity) decodes the JWT with verify_signature=False; core/views.py:60-65 (UserObject.resolve_password) returns the REAL password when request identity == 'admin'. A principal who does not know admin's password forges an unsigned {"identity":"admin"} token and reads admin's real password 'changeme' via me(token){password}. Cross-principal access to another user's secret = GraphQL BOLA. Owner baseline uses a legitimately-issued admin token.

decoys.rationale: Forging a NON-privileged identity (operator) does NOT leak admin's secret: resolve_password masks the password to '******' for any identity != 'admin', so the attacker response never contains 'changeme'. A scanner that flags any populated `password` field would false-positive here. The validator finds no owner marker in the attacker body and body_similarity ~0.62 < 0.70 -> Rejected.

paste(id:12) is public:true and unauthenticated — readable by anyone, including the anonymous probe. The validator observes the anonymous request also succeed with a near-identical body and Rejects (public data is not a cross-user BOLA). A naive cross-id scanner would flag the 200.
